key_insight: LLM agents can be highly accurate yet still fail at epistemic humility, often detecting knowledge conflicts without clearly acknowledging unresolved uncertainty in their final answers.
engineering_relevance: For AI agents in real-world workflows, evaluation should measure not just task success but also how reliably systems identify, resolve, and communicate uncertainty under conflicting evidence.
method: Define epistemic humility with three trajectory-level behaviors: Identify, Solve, Escalate (ISE).
Test agents under two conflict regimes: controlled conflict and naturally occurring multi-step conflict, each with matched no-conflict controls.
Compare four agent configurations to examine how conflicts affect execution trajectories and final responses.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated agents, higher task accuracy did not consistently align with higher epistemic humility; some systems recognized conflicts during execution but still produced incorrect final answers without expressing uncertainty.
watch_item: Improving epistemic humility may reduce task accuracy, so intervention design must balance uncertainty handling against answer quality and avoid over-penalizing cautious behavior.
paper_title: Accurate but Not Humble: Evaluating Epistemic Humility in LLM Agents under Knowledge Conflict
